title: GLMZ Citizen Benefits Bureau — Tier Advancement Protocol, Article 7.3
body:
GREAT LAKES METROPOLITAN ZONE CITIZEN BENEFITS BUREAU ADMINISTRATIVE CODE — SECTION 7, ARTICLE 3 CITIZEN TIER ADVANCEMENT AND SPONSORSHIP PROTOCOL Revision 14 | Effective Date: 2221-03-01 | Supersedes Revision 13 (2218)

---

PURPOSE

This Article establishes the formal process by which a GLMZ Citizen may petition for advancement to a higher Citizen Tier designation, the eligibility criteria governing such petitions, the role and responsibilities of Sponsoring Citizens, and the consequences of protocol violations by either party.

Tier designation determines a Citizen's access to GLMZ Citizen Benefit programs including but not limited to: Supplemental Housing Allocation, Medical Assistance Credits, Educational Access Licensing, Transit Subsidy Eligibility, Employment Placement Priority, and Nutrition Support Supplement. Tier designations are not equivalent to corponation employment classifications and should not be confused with them.

---

7.3.1 — GENERAL PROVISIONS

A Citizen's Tier is assigned at birth based on the Tier designation of their registered guardians, subject to adjustment through formal Tier Advancement Protocol (TAP) proceedings. Tier assignment may increase or decrease based on formal proceedings; it does not change automatically based on employment, income, or social circumstances unless those changes are certified through an active TAP petition.

No Citizen may advance more than one Tier level per advancement cycle. One advancement cycle is defined as five (5) calendar years. A Citizen who has been subject to a Tier Reduction Order within the preceding ten (10) years is ineligible to file a TAP petition.

---

7.3.2 — THE SPONSORSHIP REQUIREMENT

No TAP petition may be filed without the written co-signature of a Sponsoring Citizen. A Sponsoring Citizen must:

 a) Hold a Tier designation at least two (2) levels higher than the petitioning Citizen's current Tier; b) Attest, under legal oath, to the petitioning Citizen's fitness for Tier advancement; c) Agree to financial surety equal to six (6) months of the petitioning Citizen's projected Citizen Benefit increase at the requested Tier; d) Maintain an active Sponsorship Agreement with the petitioning Citizen for no fewer than thirty-six (36) months following a successful advancement.

The Sponsoring Citizen is not compensated by the GLMZ Citizens Bureau for their service. Sponsorship is considered a voluntary civic contribution.

---

7.3.3 — SPONSORSHIP AGREEMENT OBLIGATIONS

During the 36-month post-advancement Sponsorship Period, the Sponsoring Citizen assumes the following obligations:

 a) Maintain regular documented contact with the sponsored Citizen (minimum quarterly in-person meetings, with written summary filed to the Bureau within 30 days of each meeting); b) Report any Citizen Conduct Violations by the sponsored Citizen to the Bureau within 72 hours of becoming aware; c) Co-sign the sponsored Citizen's annual Tier Maintenance Attestation; d) Provide, upon Bureau request, a written assessment of the sponsored Citizen's continued fitness for their advanced Tier.

Failure to fulfill Sponsorship Agreement obligations may result in: financial penalties against the Sponsoring Citizen; retroactive recapture of Citizen Benefit increases received by the sponsored Citizen during the default period; or, in cases of documented willful non-compliance, suspension of the Sponsoring Citizen's own Tier status pending review.

---

7.3.4 — THE SPONSORING CITIZEN'S DISCRETION

Sponsor selection is entirely at the discretion of the petitioning Citizen. The Bureau does not assign, suggest, or facilitate Sponsor identification. Resources for Sponsor identification are listed in Appendix D of this Article (Bureau-approved community boards, civic networking programs, and employer-affiliated sponsorship referral services).

The Bureau notes that Sponsoring Citizens are private individuals exercising voluntary civic participation. The Bureau neither regulates nor reviews the nature of any personal relationship between a petitioning Citizen and a Sponsoring Citizen, provided that such relationships do not constitute documented coercion under Article 12.1 of the Administrative Code.

---

7.3.5 — SPONSORSHIP VIOLENCE CLASSIFICATION

Instances of assault, battery, threatening communications, property damage, or homicide in which the victim is a Sponsoring Citizen and the perpetrator is a sponsored or prospective sponsored Citizen are classified as Tier Protocol Violations under Section 14.7 of the Penal Code. Tier Protocol Violations carry mandatory minimum sentencing of twenty (20) years administrative detention and mandatory permanent Tier Reduction to Tier 1.

Sponsorship Violence incidents are compiled annually by the Bureau and submitted to the GLMZ Legislative Council as part of the Tier System Integrity Report. Note: this report is not publicly available. Access requires a minimum Tier 4 Citizen designation.

---

NOTES ON CURRENT REVISION

Revision 14 introduces the following changes from Revision 13: — Surety requirement increased from four (4) months to six (6) months (7.3.2.c) — Sponsorship Period extended from twenty-four (24) months to thirty-six (36) months (7.3.2.d) — Ineligibility period for Citizens with prior Tier Reductions increased from seven (7) to ten (10) years (7.3.1) — Classification of Sponsorship Violence incidents under Penal Code Section 14.7 added (7.3.5, new provision)

All prior Sponsorship Agreements executed under Revision 13 remain valid. Parties to active Agreements are subject to Revision 14 terms for any renewal or modification filed on or after 2221-03-01.

---

GLMZ CITIZEN BENEFITS BUREAU Administrative Division, Tier Management Office All inquiries: Citizens may submit written inquiries to their district Tier Management Office during posted business hours. In-person walk-in service is available to Tier 3 and above Citizens only. Tier 1 and Tier 2 inquiries must be submitted through the digital portal or approved community liaison organizations.
